articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities and Individuals in Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Actions
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations on November 13, 2026, targeting individuals and entities involved in counter narcotics and counter terrorism activities.

These actions aim to disrupt the financial networks of those who engage in illicit drug trafficking and support terrorist organizations, underscoring the U.S. commitment to combating these threats globally.
Further details regarding the specific individuals and entities designated, and the implications of these actions, are available on the Treasury website.

articles.headline: OFAC Updates Iran Designation List
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued an update to its Iran designation list on November 9, 2026.
This update reflects ongoing efforts to address Iran's destabilizing activities and its support for various illicit networks.
The specific changes to the designation list were not immediately detailed but are expected to impact entities and individuals connected to Iran's financial and strategic sectors.

articles.headline: New Iran-related Designations Imposed by OFAC
body: On November 6, 2026, the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations.
These designations are part of a broader strategy to exert economic pressure on Iran and target its involvement in activities deemed contrary to U.S. national security interests.
The Treasury Department's announcement provides further specifics on the entities and individuals affected by these latest measures.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Cyber, Criminal Organizations, and Cuba-Related Entities; Publishes Cuba Determination
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a series of designations on November 5, 2026, targeting cyber-related activities, transnational criminal organizations, and entities linked to Cuba.
The U.S. also issued a determination extending Executive Order 14404 to four additional sectors of the Cuban economy: manufacturing, technology, electronics, and marine.

Among the Cuba-related designations were Cuban oil shippers, state entities, and Chinese military suppliers, including China National Electronic Import and Export Company (CEIEC) and Beijing H&C Technologies Co., Ltd., a subsidiary of China Electronics Technology Group Corporation.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Iran-Related Designations, Amends Venezuela GL, and Issues Alert
body: On November 4, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations and updates to existing listings.
In addition to these actions, OFAC published an Iran-related alert and issued an amended Venezuela-related General License along with a new Frequently Asked Question.
These measures reflect the U.S. government's ongoing efforts to address perceived threats from both Iran and Venezuela through economic sanctions.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Iran-related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued an amended Iran-related General License on October 29, 2026.
General Licenses are typically issued to authorize certain transactions that would otherwise be prohibited under sanctions programs.
This amendment aims to clarify or adjust the scope of permissible activities related to Iran, and further details are available on the OFAC website.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities in North Korea and Democratic Republic of the Congo
body: On October 28, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations targeting entities in North Korea and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
These actions are part of ongoing efforts to counter illicit activities and human rights abuses in these regions.
The designations aim to disrupt financial networks supporting the proliferation of weapons and other destabilizing actions.

articles.headline: Extreme Networks, Inc. Reaches Settlement Agreement with OFAC
body: Extreme Networks, Inc. has reached a settlement agreement with the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) on October 27, 2026.
The settlement addresses alleged violations of OFAC sanctions regulations, highlighting the importance of robust compliance programs for companies operating internationally.
Further details of the settlement, including the specific violations and the agreed-upon penalty, are available through OFAC's public records.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs on Blocking, Rejecting Transactions, and Reporting
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued amended Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) on October 26, 2026, regarding blocking and rejecting transactions and filing reports with OFAC.
These amendments aim to provide clearer guidance to financial institutions and other entities on their obligations under U.S. sanctions programs.
The updated FAQs are crucial for ensuring compliance and understanding the latest interpretations of OFAC regulations.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Iran-Related Designations, Belarus and North Korea Removals, and New General Licenses
body: On October 21, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations.
Concurrently, OFAC also announced removals of certain designations related to Belarus and North Korea, indicating a recalibration of sanctions policies in those areas.
Additionally, OFAC issued new Iran-related and Russia-related General Licenses and amended existing Frequently Asked Questions to provide further guidance.

articles.headline: EU Imposes New Sanctions on Russia Targeting Financial, Energy, and E-commerce Sectors
body: The European Union foreign ministers imposed additional restrictive measures on 12 individuals and 101 entities on November 16, 2026, in response to Russia's actions in Ukraine.
The new sanctions target nearly 50 Russian banks and financial institutions, aiming to cut off financial channels that fund Russia's war effort.

The package also cracks down on Russia's e-commerce, including the sole shareholder of retail giant Wildberries and an individual controlling a majority stake in Ozon, another major Russian e-commerce company.

articles.headline: EU Sanctions 30 Individuals and Two Entities for Russia's Cyber and Hybrid Activities
body: On November 16, 2026, the Council of the European Union decided to add 30 individuals and two entities to the list of those subject to EU restrictive measures for Russia's malicious cyber activities and foreign information manipulation and interference (FIMI).

Among the sanctioned entities is the Social Design Agency (SDA), a Moscow-based public relations and political technology company accused of carrying out large-scale information manipulation projects funded and supervised by the Russian Presidential Administration.

The sanctions also target NoName057(16), a pro-Russian hacker group responsible for cyber-attacks on government bodies, critical infrastructure, and private companies in Ukraine, the United States, and EU member states.
articles.source: Council of the EU / EU NEIGHBOURS east

articles.headline: EU Imposes Anti-Dumping Duties on Cold-Rolled Flat Steel Imports
body: The European Commission imposed anti-dumping duties on imports of certain cold-rolled flat steel products from India, Japan, Taiwan, Türkiye, and Vietnam on November 16, 2026.
The definitive anti-dumping duties range from 3% to 27.9%, following an investigation that found these products were entering the EU at dumped prices.
The Commission identified particular market situations in India and Taiwan, where government measures and Chinese overcapacity, respectively, affected domestic steel prices.

articles.headline: U.S. and Thailand Reach 'Substantial Conclusion' on Reciprocal Trade Agreement
body: The United States and Thailand have reached a 'substantial conclusion' in their negotiations for a Reciprocal Trade Agreement (ART), as confirmed by President Donald J. Trump and Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul on November 17, 2026, in Manila, Philippines.
The agreement is expected to strengthen bilateral economic relations, building upon existing frameworks like the 1966 Treaty of Amity and Economic Relations.

Thailand has agreed to eliminate all tariffs on U.S. exports and remove substantial non-tariff barriers on American vehicles, medical devices, pharmaceuticals, ethanol, and poultry, and will purchase an additional $2.6 billion in U.S. agricultural products.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.
